title: SpecCloak: Probing Harmful Code Generation through Engineering Specifications
abstract: arXiv:2610.17907v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The code generation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) can equally be misused to implement harmful functionality, underscoring the need to understand their safety behavior in response to programming requests. While request phrasing is known to influence refusal, it remains unclear whether the form in which coding task requirements are stated affects the refusal process for malicious code generation. We introduce PseudoSpec, a template that organizes functional requirements as engineering specifications, and investigate its effects through controlled comparisons, representation analysis, and activation interventions. Across five open-weight models, removing explicit risk keywords only partially reduces refusal, whereas specification prompting substantially lowers refusal even when these keywords are retained. translated_title: SpecCloak：通过工程规格探测有害代码生成
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）的代码生成能力同样可能被滥用以实现有害功能，这凸显了理解模型在响应编程请求时安全行为的必要性。虽然已知请求的措辞会影响模型的拒绝行为，但目前尚不清楚编码任务需求以何种形式表述会影响恶意代码生成的拒绝过程。我们提出了PseudoSpec，一个将功能需求组织为工程规格的模板，并通过受控比较、表示分析和激活干预来研究其影响。在五个开源权重模型上的实验表明，仅移除显式的风险关键词只能部分降低拒绝率，而规格化提示即使在这些关键词被保留的情况下也能显著降低拒绝率。这种拒绝率的降低伴随着模型内部表示向代码输出相关方向的一致性偏移，且沿该方向的激活干预（注：摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出PseudoSpec模板，发现将恶意代码需求伪装成工程规格的形式可以显著绕过LLM的安全拒绝机制，即使保留风险关键词也能大幅降低拒绝率。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes PseudoSpec, showing that framing malicious coding requirements as engineering specifications substantially bypasses LLM refusal mechanisms, even when explicit risk keywords are retained.
